en: Yahya ibn Ayyub, 'Amr an-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb all narrated to me from Ibn 'Ulayyah—and the wording is that of 'Amr—who said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said on the Day of Sacrifice: 'Whoever slaughtered before the prayer must repeat it.' A man stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is a day in which meat is craved,' and he mentioned something regarding his neighbors, as if the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) believed him. He said: 'And I have a young female goat (jadha'ah) that is dearer to me than two sheep of meat; may I sacrifice it?' He granted him permission. He [Muhammad] said: I do not know whether his permission extended to anyone other than him or not. He said: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) turned towards two rams and slaughtered them, and the people got up and went to a small flock of sheep and divided them among themselves—or he said: shared them out.

And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me; (Second Chain) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi reported to us: Shu'bah narrated to us with this chain of transmission, and he did not mention the doubt in his saying: 'It is better than a mature one (musinnah).'

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Salamah, from Abu Juhayfah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: Abu Burdah slaughtered before the prayer, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Replace it.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing except a young female goat (jadha'ah)'—Shu'bah said: and I think he said—'and it is better than a mature one (musinnah).' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Put it in its place, but it will never suffice for anyone after you.'

Ahmad ibn Sa'id ibn Sakhr ad-Darimi narrated to me: Abu an-Nu'man 'Arim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahid—meaning Ibn Ziyad—narrated to us: 'Asim al-Ahwal narrated to us, from ash-Sha'bi: al-Bara' ibn 'Azib narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice, saying: 'No one should sacrifice until he has prayed.' A man said: 'I have a young female goat (a milch kid) that is better than two sheep of meat.' He said: 'Then sacrifice it, but a young female goat (jadha'ah) will not suffice for anyone after you.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Hannad ibn as-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us; (Second Chain) and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim both narrated from Jarir; both of them from Mansur, from ash-Sha'bi, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) delivered a sermon to us on the Day of Sacrifice after the prayer. Then he mentioned something similar to their hadith.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Zubayd, who heard ash-Sha'bi, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna—narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Zubayd al-Iyami, from ash-Sha'bi, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is that we pray, then we return and offer the sacrifice. So whoever does that has acted according to our Sunnah; and whoever slaughters before that, it is merely meat that he has provided for his family, and has nothing to do with the sacrifice.' And Abu Burdah ibn Niyar had slaughtered, so he said: 'I have a young female goat (jadha'ah) that is better than a mature one (musinnah).' He said: 'Slaughter it, but it will never suffice for anyone after you.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us, from Firas, from 'Amir, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Whoever prays our prayer, faces our Qiblah, and offers our sacrifice, let him not slaughter until he has prayed.' My maternal uncle said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I offered the sacrifice on behalf of a son of mine.' He said: 'That was something you hastened for your family.' He said: 'I have a sheep that is better than two sheep.' He said: 'Sacrifice it, for it is the best sacrifice.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from ash-Sha'bi, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) delivered a sermon to us on the Day of Sacrifice, saying: 'None of you should slaughter until he has prayed.' He said: My maternal uncle said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is a day in which meat is desired.' Then he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of Hushaym.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym reported to us, from Dawud, from ash-Sha'bi, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: that his maternal uncle, Abu Burdah ibn Niyar, slaughtered before the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) slaughtered. So he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is a day in which meat is desired, and I hastened my sacrifice to feed my family, my neighbors, and the people of my household.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Repeat the sacrifice.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have a young female goat (a milch kid) that is better than two sheep of meat.' He said: 'It is the better of your two sacrifices, but a young goat (jadha'ah) will not suffice for anyone after you.'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah reported to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Amir, from al-Bara', who said: My maternal uncle Abu Burdah sacrificed before the prayer, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'That is a sheep of meat.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have a young female goat (jadha'ah) from the goats.' He said: 'Sacrifice it, but it is not valid for anyone other than you.' Then he said: 'Whoever sacrifices before the prayer has only slaughtered for himself, and whoever slaughters after the prayer has completed his sacrifice and conformed to the Sunnah of the Muslims.'
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us with this chain of transmission the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Aswad, who heard Jundab al-Bajali say: I was present with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when he prayed on the day of Adha, then delivered a sermon and said: 'Whoever slaughtered before he prayed must slaughter another in its place, and whoever has not slaughtered should slaughter in the name of Allah.'

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated it to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us from Ibn 'Uyaynah; both of them from al-Aswad ibn Qays with this chain of transmission, and both said: 'in the name of Allah (ala ismi-llah),' like the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas Sallam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Jundab ibn Sufyan, who said: I attended the Adha prayer with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). When he concluded his prayer with the people, he looked at some sheep that had already been slaughtered and said: 'Whoever slaughtered before the prayer must slaughter a sheep in its place, and whoever has not slaughtered should slaughter in the name of Allah.'

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: al-Aswad ibn Qays narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Abu Khaythamah reported to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays: Jundab ibn Sufyan narrated to me, saying: I attended the Adha with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). No sooner had he prayed and finished his prayer and said the taslim, than he saw meat of sacrificial animals that had been slaughtered before he finished his prayer. So he said: 'Whoever had slaughtered his sacrifice before he prayed—or before we prayed—must slaughter another in its place, and whoever had not slaughtered should slaughter in the name of Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj; (Second Chain) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bakr reported to us: Ibn Jurayj reported to us; (Third Chain) and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu az-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that any animal be tied up and killed (sabran).

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us: Abu Bishr reported to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Umar passed by some young men of Quraysh who had set up a bird and were shooting at it, having agreed with the owner of the bird that he would have every missed arrow from their shots. When they saw Ibn 'Umar, they dispersed. Ibn 'Umar said: 'Who did this? May Allah curse whoever did this! Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) cursed whoever takes anything possessing a soul as a target.'

Shayban ibn Farrukh and Abu Kamil—and the wording is that of Abu Kamil—narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Umar passed by a group of people who had set up a hen and were shooting arrows at it. When they saw Ibn 'Umar, they dispersed away from it. Ibn 'Umar said: 'Who did this? Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) cursed whoever did this.'
And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not take anything possessing a soul as a target.'

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id and 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Yahya ibn Habib narrated to me: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us; (Third Chain) and Abu Kuraib narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Hisham ibn Zayd ibn Anas ibn Malik say: I entered the house of al-Hakam ibn Ayyub along with my grandfather Anas ibn Malik, and there were people who had tied up a hen and were shooting at it. He said: So Anas said: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that animals be tied up and killed (sabran).'

And Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Hushaym narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahhab ath-Thaqafi reported to us; (Third Chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; (Fourth Chain) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf reported to us, from Sufyan; (Fifth Chain) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir reported to us, from Mansur; all of them from Khalid al-Hadhdha', with the chain of transmission of the hadith of Ibn 'Ulayyah and the meaning of his hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: There are two things I memorized from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: 'Indeed, Allah has prescribed excellence in all things. So when you kill, kill well; and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each one of you sharpen his blade and let him give ease to his slaughtered animal.'
And Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated it to us: ath-Thaqafi narrated to us, from Ayyub, with this chain of transmission, something similar to it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that a relative of 'Abdullah ibn Mughaffal flicked pebbles (with his fingers). He said: So he forbade him and said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade flicking pebbles, saying: 'It does not hunt game, nor does it inflict injury on an enemy, but it breaks a tooth and puts out an eye.' He said: Then he did it again. So he said: 'I tell you that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade it, and then you flick pebbles? I will never speak to you again!'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from 'Uqbah ibn Suhban, from 'Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade flicking pebbles. Ibn Ja'far said in his narration: And he said: 'It does not inflict injury on an enemy, nor does it kill game, but it breaks a tooth and puts out an eye.' And Ibn Mahdi said: 'It does not inflict injury on an enemy,' and he did not mention: 'and puts out an eye.'
Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Ma'bad narrated to me: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us: Kahmas reported to us with this chain of transmission something similar to it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Kahmas narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal saw a man from his companions flicking pebbles, so he said to him: 'Do not flick pebbles, for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) disliked—or he said: forbade—flicking pebbles; for game cannot be hunted with it, nor can an enemy be injured by it, but it breaks a tooth and puts out an eye.' Then he saw him flicking pebbles after that, so he said to him: 'I inform you that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) disliked or forbade flicking pebbles, and then I see you flicking pebbles? I will not speak a word to you for such-and-such a time!'
